en.title: Soft C Before E and I
en.summary: You pronounce the letter c like ch in church before the vowels e and i.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: You say this sound like the start of the English word 'church'. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks the air. This sound is a voiceless consonant. A voiceless sound is a sound where the voice is off. Listen to (cer) /tʃer/, which means sky.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Put the front of your tongue behind your top teeth. Stop the air in your mouth for one moment. Blow the air through your teeth. Push your lips forward slightly as you speak. Do not use your voice during this sound.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: A letter is a written sign of the alphabet. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch. Look at the letter c in a word. You make this sound when c comes before the vowels e or i. You see this rule in (cer) /tʃer/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say the sound of k in the English word 'cat'. Do not say the sound of s in the English word 'sun'. Touch your tongue to the roof behind your teeth first. Release the air quickly and do not use your voice. Listen to the clear sound in (cer) /tʃer/.
